body.statement: For a directed acyclic graph that is a disjoint union of directed edges, the multivariate restricted additive-noise condition in Peters et al.'s Definition 27 specializes to the conjunction of their bivariate Condition 19 over the edges; under that condition their Theorem 28 identifies the directed acyclic graph from the observational law.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 28 Let L(X) = L(X1, . . . , Xp) be generated by a restricted additive noise model with graph G0 and let L(X) satisfy causal minimality with respect to G0, i.e., the functions fj are not constant (Proposition 17). Then, G0 is identifiable from the joint distribution.

attestation.note: Literal theorem statement verified in the primary JMLR PDF, Peters et al. (2014), volume 15, page 2025 (PDF page 16), https://jmlr.org/papers/volume15/peters14a/peters14a.pdf. Immediately preceding Definition 27 defines restricted ANM by requiring the indicated conditional bivariate triple to satisfy Condition 19 for every j, parent i, and admissible S. For a disjoint union of edges, block independence makes this requirement specialize edgewise.
